note: Hand-checked data center deals, corporate tax breaks and corporate lobbying of NY town, village and city officials. Each entry cites the public sources it was checked against. In New York most of these deals are granted by an industrial development agency (IDA); they are listed under the government whose taxes the deal cuts, with the IDA named. Proposed deals that have not been approved (for example the Stream data center at STAMP in the Town of Alabama, paused by the July 2026 state moratorium) are left out. Applied by scripts/common/red-flags.mjs.

deals.label: Data center tax break (PILOT)
deals.detail: JPMorgan Chase's Orangeburg data center has had a payment-in-lieu-of-taxes (PILOT) deal covering county, town and school taxes since 2017. In February 2024 the Rockland County IDA approved nearly $77 million more in tax breaks for a roughly $1 billion expansion that promises exactly one permanent job.

sources.label: New York Focus: This data center is getting a $77 million tax break to create one job (April 20, 2026)

deals.label: Data center tax break (PILOT)
deals.detail: The Lockport Industrial Development Agency gave Yahoo's data center ten years without property taxes on each of two phases (approved 2009 and 2013) and up to $200 million in sales-tax breaks on equipment over 20 years. Total public subsidies were estimated at up to $478 million, about $2.4 million per job.

deals.label: Corporate tax break (warehouse)
deals.detail: In February 2021 the Hamburg Industrial Development Agency approved a $6.85 million incentive package for an Amazon warehouse, cutting at least $2.2 million in property taxes over ten years. As of July 2023 the site had created no jobs.

sources.label: NY Assemblymember Jonathan Rivera: call for IDA reform over Amazon warehouse school tax abatements
